title: Integer-Quantized Hierarchical Matrices with Adaptive Bit Allocation
summary: We present an adaptive bitwidth allocation method for quantizing low-rank factors in hierarchical matrices in order to decrease storage while meeting a given constraint on their reconstruction error. For the bitwidth allocation we formulate a discrete storage minimization problem and show that an optimal assignment can give larger singular values at least as many bits as smaller ones. We further develop a greedy algorithm that meets the specified max-norm quantization error budget. We investigate a hierarchical block partition in which all of the non-diagonal blocks are represented by quantized low-rank factors and only dense blocks remain dense; in this way a global reconstruction bound related to $η_k$ and $R_k$ is obtained, with the former and latter being bounds on the truncation and reconstruction arithmetic errors, respectively. Extensive simulations, carried out with kernel and BEM matrices under block-relative budgets, indicate that the proposed method achieves a reduction in storage of up to $44.3\times$ when compared to storing the complete matrix densely in FP64, and a reduction of up to $5.70\times$ when compared to the FP64 low-rank factors within the same partition, together with measured reconstruction errors that remained below the maximum norm bounds in all the hierarchical tests.

title: Beyond atol and rtol: Sound Test Oracles for Low-Precision GPU Kernels
summary:
Low-precision GPU kernels are commonly tested against a reference using hand-picked absolute and relative tolerances. Legitimate numerical error varies with the input, format and precision plan, so a fixed tolerance trades false alarms for missed faults. We present numoracle, which derives per-element acceptance regions from precision-annotated reference programs. Its calculus tracks shared rounding errors, provenance-ordered products, block-scaled quantizers and calibrated math-library errors. A rounding-interval check detects faulty stores that symmetric bounds can admit. Soundness is conditional on explicit rounding, hardware, domain and implementation assumptions; a fixed-input mode removes the zero-mean rounding assumption.
We evaluate 13 Triton operators from Liger-Kernel, Unsloth and vLLM on two GPU generations. The main campaigns produce no false alarm on 33,960 correct-kernel and behavior-preserving-variant runs per GPU. Under input shift, the GPU campaigns record no false alarm while tuned tolerances flag up to 30% of correct runs; final-version reference checks identify inputs without complete finite-range certificates. On the RTX PRO 6000, numoracle kills 116 of 124 effective mutants, versus 59-83 for four fixed baselines. Among 400 tuned tolerance configurations, requiring at most 1% false alarms in every evaluated Liger input group permits at most 31 of 53 main-mutant kills, versus numoracle's 50. Historical replays expose accuracy faults in eight change pairs without rejecting their matched corrected controls; a ninth change concerns rounding parity.

title: cuPDQPx: A GPU-Accelerated Restarted Halpern PDHG for Large-Scale Convex Quadratic Programming
summary: We present cuPDQPx, a GPU-accelerated, factorization-free first-order solver for large-scale convex quadratic programming (QP). Building on the restarted reflected Halpern primal-dual framework of cuPDLPx, we introduce an auxiliary-variable splitting that yields explicit updates without linearizing the quadratic objective or solving inner quadratic subproblems. A preconditioned proximal point interpretation yields both sublinear and linear fixed-point residual convergence guarantees. For practical efficiency, cuPDQPx integrates diagonal preconditioning, step-size selection, adaptive restart, and adaptive primal and quadratic weight updates. cuPDQPx is implemented in C and CUDA with optimized sparse matrix-vector products, kernel fusion, and CUDA Graphs. title: survivalGPU: Scalable Survival Analysis for R and Python
summary: This paper introduces survivalGPU, a high-performance Python and R package designed to accelerate survival analysis computations using graphics processing units (GPUs). While the Cox proportional hazards model remains a cornerstone of survival analysis, it can impose substantial computational burdens when applied to large longitudinal data sets. To address this limitation, survivalGPU implements Cox proportional hazards models and weighted cumulative exposure (WCE) models in Python, using PyTorch and KeOps for efficient back-end computation, with interfaces in both Python and R. Numerical validation shows that survivalGPU reproduces the results of reference implementations within the tolerances expected for the selected floating-point precision, with relative errors below 10 -2 in float32 and below 10 -5 in float64. Benchmark experiments demonstrate substantial speedups. For Cox models, coxphGPU() was 5.6x faster than coxph() from the survival package on 1,000,000 patients, and 14.0x faster based on runtimes extrapolated to 1,000 bootstrap replicates on 100,000 patients. Gains were larger for WCE models: wceGPU() was 920.7x faster than WCE() from the WCE package on 100,000 patients, and 1,321.4x faster based on runtimes extrapolated to 1,000 bootstrap replicates. These results show that survivalGPU makes flexible time-dependent survival modeling and bootstrap-based estimation of confidence intervals feasible for large-scale pharmacoepidemiological applications.

title: diff-soup: GPU-native Differentiable Simulation and Inference for Large-scale Stiff Dynamical Systems
summary: Learning physical models from spatiotemporal data requires simulating systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) and differentiating through their solution. Upon spatial discretization, these models give rise to stiff dynamical systems that require repeatedly solving large, sparse linear systems. Traditional scientific computing frameworks are largely CPU-based and require problem-specific tuning to accelerate, scale, and differentiate. In this work, we introduce diff-soup, a differentiable, sparse-oriented, unified PDE suite for GPU-native simulation and inference of large, stiff dynamical systems. Built in JAX, diff-soup provides 1) a fully differentiable design for problems with sparse structure, 2) scaling to large problems through the NVIDIA cuDSS sparse direct solver with model and data multi-GPU parallelism, and 3) end-to-end PDE-constrained optimization, from classical statistical inference to embedded deep learning. On stiff PDE benchmarks, diff-soup outperforms established CPU- and GPU-based frameworks by one to two orders of magnitude in both forward solves and gradients. We demonstrate both a classical Bayesian inference workflow, identifying constitutive relationships, and a modern deep learning workflow, training a neural field for the catalyst activity of a three-dimensional packed bed reactor. We provide diff-soup as an open-source repository to facilitate research in computational science and engineering.

title: Automatic Certified Differentiation in Lean
summary:
Automatic differentiation (the automatic computation of numerical function derivatives) has many applications, especially in scientific computing and machine learning. Several approaches to automate the calculation of derivatives have been presented. Common challenges facing those approaches include (1) having to define derivative rules for different classes of functions, (2) having to manipulate program symbols to understand the semantics of the function being differentiated, and construct the derivative function, and (3), more importantly, ensuring that the calculated derivative is correct.
In this paper, we present an approach for automatic \emph{certified} differentiation using the Lean proof assistant. By certified, we mean a correctness certificate is computed together with the derivative function and a domain on which the derivative is guaranteed to be valid. Our approach leverages existing derivative theorems included in the Mathlib Lean library instead of having to define our own rules. We also utilize Lean metaprogramming to manipulate the symbolic structure of the input function, and to construct the derivative function. The correctness certificate is computed step-wise as we apply Mathlib theorems. To make the search efficient, we index the derivative theorems by the function they differentiate. We evaluate our approach on 500 randomly generated functions: with the index, all of them are differentiated, with a median time of 0.18\,s per function, 8.6 times faster than without the index.

title: Propose-Filter-Release: Scaling Noise to Typical Sensitivity via Private Filtering
summary:
An estimator can be accurate and stable on typical data, yet sensitive to a few possible records. Differentially private mechanisms commonly scale their noise to the worst-case influence of a single record, which lets these records dictate the noise even when the remaining data would allow far less. Removing them first would restore the smaller scale, but the removal must itself be private.
We introduce \emph{propose-filter-release} (PFR), which, by privately filtering its input, turns a mechanism that protects the addition or removal of a typical record, one that fits the remaining data, into one that is differentially private in the standard sense, on every input. Using our novel filtering step, PFR requires only a concave friendliness score, which measures how well a record fits a dataset, and a release mechanism that is friendly-DP, that is, private when the changed record fits the remaining data. For every such score and release mechanism, it guarantees differential privacy under public conditions on the number of records, so it is a general privacy primitive, comparable to propose-test-release, and FriendlyCore can be viewed as one of its implementations.
We illustrate the generality of PFR by instantiating it for scalar statistics, principal subspace estimation, the KL divergence of user histograms, the effective resistances of a graph, and treatment-rule selection.

title: Adaptive Scenario Generation for KL-DRO Around a Learned Density Model
summary: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) hedges data-driven two-stage stochastic programs against error in the distribution estimated from a finite record, and standard ambiguity sets differ in how they treat realizations absent from that record. A divergence ball around the empirical distribution contains only reweightings of the record, whereas a transport ball also contains distributions supported off the record, including on realizations the data-generating process cannot produce, against which the decision is then hedged as well. We instead propose a Kullback-Leibler (KL) ball centered at a density model fitted to the record, the learned nominal, which lets the adversary up-weight costly unobserved realizations in proportion to the probability the model assigns them. Solving the resulting problem poses a second difficulty, because it can accommodate only a few scenarios, and an independent sample of that size is likely to omit the rare realizations on which the worst case concentrates. We therefore build the scenario set adaptively, alternating between solving the finite problem and drawing new realizations from the learned nominal, steered toward the worst case at the current decision, with importance weights that correct the draws back to the model. On a multi-item newsvendor problem and a capacity expansion problem on realistic grid data, centering the ball at the learned nominal rather than at the record lowers cost under distribution shift, at comparable in-distribution cost, when the record is scarce and the model class captures structure that lets it extrapolate beyond the record. The advantage fades as the record grows or as the shift departs from the structure the model has learned.

title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
summary: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. Here, we introduce world2vec to learn mechanistic world models without reward information directly from observations and actions. World2vec learns latent dynamics that faithfully reproduce the true system over long prediction horizons, with at least one order of magnitude fewer parameters than DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and LeWM. This enables state of the art performance in controlling continuous environments from pixels and accurate system identification across a benchmark of 71 attractors, demonstrating how world models are amenable to scientific discovery.

title: An ODE-based Sampler for Discrete Diffusion Models
summary: The marginals of a continuous diffusion model can be reproduced by a deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE), known as the probability flow ODE, which provides a foundation for accelerated sampling and consistency distillation. In this paper we address the question whether an analogous formulation exists for discrete diffusion models and answer it affirmatively by introducing exponential residual flows (ERFs). Our framework augments the discrete state with a continuous residual variable for each token and position. These residuals evolve deterministically according to piecewise-defined ODEs whose vector fields depend on the current discrete state and the forward and backward rate matrices of the prescribed diffusion model. The discrete state changes whenever a residual reaches zero. We prove that this construction preserves the marginals of the original diffusion. We derive a practical discretization of our sampler and specialize it to masked and uniform diffusion. The deterministic trajectories of ERFs support consistency distillation and yield empirical improvements over previous approaches across a variety of benchmarks including code and text generation tasks.

title: Multistatic ISAC with Deep Learning-Based Clutter Suppression for 5G and Beyond
summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) systems using 5G and beyond signals of opportunity enable joint wireless sensing and communication using shared infrastructure and spectrum resources. While multistatic ISAC can increase sensing coverage with spatially distributed receivers, dense and dynamic clutter can significantly degrade bistatic range and Doppler estimation, leading to errors in target localization and velocity estimation. This paper presents a multistatic ISAC framework with clutter suppression for high-fidelity estimation of target position and velocity. Distributed clutter is modeled with randomly located scatterers with varying Doppler spreads and radar cross sections to capture dense and dynamic clutter effects. A broad range of conventional signal processing baselines are evaluated for clutter suppression, showing limited robustness under strong clutter conditions. To address this limitation, deep learning-based clutter suppression methods are introduced to improve robustness against dense and dynamic clutter by employing residual and attention-enhanced deep neural network architectures that directly enhance target responses from clutter-contaminated observations. These methods substantially outperform conventional approaches in target position and velocity estimation across diverse clutter conditions in multistatic ISAC.

title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
summary: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified training system that mixes static data and RL generations within a single trainer. Across controlled and real-world experiments, unified training improves the accuracy-compute tradeoff and task coverage while preserving broader capabilities, and provides a stronger starting point for continual learning. This work lays the groundwork for a unified science of foundation-model training, connecting mathematical principles, training infrastructure, and the development of model capabilities.

title: Engineering structural tunability in MOF-based photocatalysts for efficient CO 2  photoreduction
summary:
Abstract
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer an exceptional platform for photocatalytic CO2 reduction (CO2RR) because metal nodes, organic linkers, defects and pore microenvironments can be engineered to integrate CO2 capture and light-driven redox chemistry. Yet, the intrinsic trade-offs of many pristine MOFs, limited conductivity, short carrier diffusion lengths, and framework instability under operating conditions often cap activity and selectivity. This review summarizes recent advances in MOF-based photocatalysts, focusing on the integration of MOFs with semiconductors, metal cocatalysts and plasmonic components to optimize band alignment, facilitate interfacial charge transfer and construct efficient catalytic microenvironments. Progress is discussed by major C1 products (CO, CH4, CH3OH and HCOOH), with emphasis on how node/linker electronics, defect chemistry, pore polarity and heterointerfaces govern CO2 activation, intermediate stabilization and product-determining pathways. We critically examine the correlation between enhanced CO2 adsorption and the higher photoreduction rates, and the dominant roles of mass transport and interfacial kinetics. Finally, we summarize emerging AI and machine-learning strategies for accelerating materials discovery and mechanistic understanding, and outline key challenges and opportunities toward scalable, selective and durable MOF-based CO2 photoconversion.

content_preview:
Abstract
Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer an exceptional platform for photocatalytic CO2 reduction (CO2RR) because metal nodes, organic linkers, defects and pore microenvironments can be engineered to integrate CO2 capture and light-driven redox chemistry. Yet, the intrinsic trade-offs of many pristine MOFs, limited conductivity, short carrier diffusion lengths, and framework instability under operating conditions often cap activity and selectivity. This review summarizes recent advances in MOF-based photocatalysts, focusing on the integration of MOFs with semiconductors, metal cocatalysts and plasmonic components to optimize band alignment, facilitate interfacial charge transfer and construct efficient catalytic microenvironments. Progress is discussed by major C1 products (CO, CH4, CH3OH and HCOOH), with emphasis on how node/linker electronics, defect chemistry, pore polarity and heterointerfaces govern CO2 activation, intermediate stabilization and product-determining pathways. We critically examine the correlation between enhanced CO2 adsorption and the higher photoreduction rates, and the dominant roles of mass transport and interfacial kinetics. Finally, we summarize emerging AI and machine-learning strategies for accelerating materials discovery and mechanistic understanding, and outline key challenges and opportunities toward scalable, selective and durable MOF-based CO2 photoconversion.

title: ARISMA: Guidelines for AI- and LLM-Assisted Systematic Reviews, Scoping Reviews, and Mapping Studies
summary:
Abstract
Systematic reviews, scoping reviews, mapping studies, and related evidence syntheses are increasingly difficult to conduct with fully manual workflows as search volumes, update cycles, and synthesis requirements continue to expand. At the same time, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and large language models are rapidly entering review practice across query formulation, screening, extraction, categorization, appraisal support, and reporting. Yet the empirical evidence remains uneven, task-dependent, and insufficient to justify unconstrained automation. Existing standards such as PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, PRISMA-ScR, PRISMA-P, PRESS, and SWiM remain essential, but none provides an end-to-end operational standard for when AI use is methodologically appropriate, how it should be validated, which review decisions must remain human-led, and how AI involvement should be reported so that readers can audit it. This paper proposes ARISMA, an AI Reporting and Integration standard for Systematic Methods and Analysis. ARISMA treats AI as an inspected, benchmarked, logged, and reversible assistant rather than an autonomous reviewer. It is built around one governing principle: every consequential scientific decision must remain human-interpretable, human-auditable, and human-accountable. title: Trust but Verify: Introducing DAVinCI – A Framework for Dual Attribution and Verification in Claim Inference for Language Models
summary:
Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable fluency and versatility across a wide range of NLP tasks, yet they remain prone to factual inaccuracies and hallucinations. This limitation poses significant risks in high-stakes domains such as healthcare, law, and scientific communication, where trust and verifiability are paramount. In this paper, we introduce DAVinCI - a Dual Attribution and Verification framework designed to enhance the factual reliability and interpretability of LLM outputs. DAVinCI operates in two stages: (i) it attributes generated claims to internal model components and external sources; (ii) it verifies each claim using entailment-based reasoning and confidence calibration. We evaluate DAVinCI across multiple datasets, including FEVER and CLIMATE-FEVER, and compare its performance against standard verification-only baselines. Our results show that DAVinCI significantly improves classification accuracy, attribution precision, recall, and F1-score by 5-20%. Through an extensive ablation study, we isolate the contributions of evidence span selection, recalibration thresholds, and retrieval quality. We also release a modular DAVinCI implementation that can be integrated into existing LLM pipelines. By bridging attribution and verification, DAVinCI offers a scalable path to auditable, trustworthy AI systems. This work contributes to the growing effort to make LLMs not only powerful but also accountable.

title: GRASP: GRanularity-Aware Search Policy for Agentic RAG
summary: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) extends static RAG by allowing language models to iteratively reason, generate search queries, retrieve evidence, and predict answers. However, it remains challenging for models to decide when to retrieve, whether to use lexical matching or semantic similarity, and how to control context granularity to prevent irrelevant tokens from interfering with agent reasoning. In this paper, we introduce GRASP, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for training agents to adaptively coordinate complementary retrieval tools during multi-step reasoning. GRASP provides the agent with semantic search, keyword search, and paragraph-reading actions, enabling it to retrieve sentence-level evidence and expand further context only when needed. We train the policy with a reward that jointly accounts for answer accuracy, grounded reading, complementary search, and turn efficiency. Experiments on multi-hop reasoning benchmarks show that GRASP improves both retrieval recall and downstream question answering performance compared with single-step retrieval, prompting-based agentic RAG, and RL-based retrieval baselines. Qualitative and ablation analyses show that the learned policy develops interpretable skimming and scanning behavior: it uses semantic search for broad exploration, paragraph reading for local verification, and keyword search for entity-specific evidence. title: CRISP: Cliff-aware Residual-free Input-adaptive Sparse Prefilling with Entropy-Motivated Routing
summary:
The attention prefilling phase of long-context LLM inference scales quadratically, making self-attention a severe computational bottleneck. Traditional sparse attention methods mitigate this through fixed patterns or offline profiling, but lack the flexibility to adapt to input-dependent attention structure. Recent dynamic methods address this by routing heads to sparse patterns in real-time, but rely on indirect routing proxies with overhead and budget allocation mechanisms that overlook the post-softmax mass hierarchy. We present CRISP (Cliff-aware Residual-free Input-adaptive Sparse Prefilling), which identifies and addresses two structural challenges in this dynamic routing paradigm.

title: Not Worth Another Token: Marginal Value Estimation for Efficient Deep Research Agents
summary:
Long-horizon research agents solve open-ended tasks through iterative retrieval, aggregation, and synthesis, but context grows rapidly while the marginal value of additional evidence often declines. This leads to unnecessary token cost, higher latency, and noisier inputs for final report generation. We study marginal value estimation for context management in deep research agents and present the first systematic stage-aware comparison of pruning strategies across the pipeline. We evaluate lightweight heuristic criteria and a learned value model at pre-retrieval, post-retrieval, and pre-synthesis stages. Our results show that pruning effectiveness depends more on where pruning is applied than on the specific scoring rule: early pruning yields the largest end-to-end savings, while later pruning mainly refines the final synthesis context. Lightweight heuristics reduce token usage by up to 73% with little quality degradation, learned pruning remains competitive on selected trade-offs, and no single method dominates across quality, efficiency, and faithfulness. These findings provide practical guidance for designing efficient long-horizon agentic systems.

title: Myocardial remodeling and fibrosis by cardiovascular magnetic resonance in adults with congenital aortic valve stenosis
summary:
Left ventricular (LV) remodeling is becoming increasingly important in assessing the impact of aortic stenosis (AS). However, data on structural LV remodeling in congenital AS patients is scarce. Therefore, this study aimed to describe LV remodeling before and after aortic valve replacement (AVR) in adults with congenital AS and identify markers associated with myocardial fibrosis.
METHODS AND RESULTS:
In this prospective study, adult patients with congenital AS were included with 1) at least mild AS (Vmax ≥2.5 m/s) or 2) prior AVR due to congenital AS. Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance (CMR) was performed to assess structural LV remodeling. Results were compared with CMR data from 20 healthy controls. Data from 73 patients were included (median age 43 [30-52] years, 67% male), of whom 20 patients were post-AVR. LV systolic function was preserved in all patients. LV mass index was significantly higher in patients with a native valve than in controls (70 ± 19 vs. 59 ± 8 g/m2, p = 0.023). Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) was present in 19 patients (26%): 13 with a native valve and 6 post-AVR (25% vs. 30%, p = 0.64). Native T1 and extracellular volume (ECV) did not differ significantly from healthy controls. In patients post-AVR, LV mass index and matrix volume were significantly lower compared to patients with a native valve.
CONCLUSION:

title: Oracle's Always-Free Tier: The Server Everyone Forgets
summary:
Oracle's Always-Free Tier: The Server Everyone Forgets
Oracle Cloud quietly gives away a permanent 4-core, 24GB-RAM ARM server that would cost $80-100/month on AWS. Here's why signups get rejected, the region choice you can't undo, and how to actually get the machine.
Every guide to standing up your first server starts in the same place: pick a droplet, enter a card, pay five dollars a month, scale up when you outgrow it. That's fine advice, and for a solo builder pre-revenue it's also five dollars a month you didn't need to spend. Because there's a machine sitting one signup away that costs nothing and never stops being free — and almost nobody claims it, because the signup quietly rejects a large fraction of the people who try.
Oracle's Always Free tier is the most under-used piece of infrastructure available to an early-stage founder. Not a 12-month trial that flips to billing on month 13. A permanent grant, alive for as long as your account is alive. The spec is genuinely absurd for the price, and the price is zero.
What you actually get
The headline resource is an ARM server built on Ampere A1 cores. Oracle meters it by the hour — 3,000 OCPU-hours and 18,000 GB-hours per month — which sounds abstract until you do the division: it's exactly enough to run one always-on machine with 4 cores and 24GB of RAM, around the clock, forever. Add 200GB of block storage and 10TB of monthly outbound traffic, and you have a development box that most people would assume costs real money.
It does cost real money — somewhere else. Here's the same configuration priced on the majors:
| Spec | Oracle Always Free | AWS (on-demand, roughly equivalent) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 ARM cores / 24GB RAM | $0/month | ~$80-100/month |
| 200GB block storage | included | ~$20/month |
| 10TB egress/month | included | egress billed per-GB after 100GB |

Add 200GB of block storage and 10TB of monthly outbound traffic, and you have a development box that most people would assume costs real money.
It does cost real money — somewhere else. Here's the same configuration priced on the majors:
| Spec | Oracle Always Free | AWS (on-demand, roughly equivalent) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 ARM cores / 24GB RAM | $0/month | ~$80-100/month |
| 200GB block storage | included | ~$20/month |
| 10TB egress/month | included | egress billed per-GB after 100GB |

title: 当 AI 能读懂二进制，闭源软件还剩多少护城河？
summary:
🤖 AI 中文摘要 ✓ 基于全文
开源项目 REA 将 Claude Code、Codex 等编码智能体通过 MCP 接入 Ghidra、Hopper、IDA，支持二进制、Electron/JavaScript 与 .NET 静态分析，GitHub Star 超 20 万。展示案例覆盖 Notion、经典游戏函数重建等，引发 HN 对“是否只是封装 Ghidra”的讨论。其意义在于 AI Agent 工具链向逆向工程扩展，并带来闭源软件护城河、独立开发者被复制与安全边界等争议。
📡 相关内容（按标签重合度）
-   📰GitHub新晋顶流REA：当大模型能逆向一切，软件行业还剩什么？ GitHub 项目 REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）数日揽 12 万星，用 TypeScript 编写并以 MIT 开源，通过 MCP 让 Claude Code、Codex 等编程 Agent 调用 Ghidra、Hopper、IDA，逆向原生二进制、Electron、APK、.NET 等并复现功能。文章据此讨论 AI 逆向工程对闭源护城河的冲击、克隆潮，以及软件价值向服务、know-how 与客户关系转移。
-   📰一周 10 万星，AI「逆向一切」，但大家不要过于兴奋 REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）一周涨超10万星，通过MCP把Ghidra/IDA等逆向工具接入Claude Code、Codex等智能体，可自动分析二进制并复刻功能。文章强调其技术并非全新，但大幅降低逆向门槛，并引发版权、商业秘密、净室开发与数据外泄等合规争议。对关注AI Agent、MCP和产品级AI应用的人有参考价值，但需警惕炒作。
-   📰Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries REA 是一个开源、本地运行的逆向工程 Agent 工具，通过 MCP 让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等代理检查原生二进制、JS/Electron、.NET、Web 与 Android 等目标，并返回证据和限制。它支持 npx rea-agents setup 快速注册到代理，也可用 CLI 直接分析，原生分析可接入 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA。适合关注 AI Agent、MCP、开源开发工具和安全逆向的用户。
-   📰逆向一切的REA，正让“Photoshop们”瑟瑟发抖？ 开源项目REA通过MCP把Ghidra、IDA等逆向工具封装为AI Agent可调用接口，让普通开发者也能让Claude Code、Codex等自动分析闭源软件并复刻功能。文章梳理其能力边界：成功多集中在小程序或单一功能，难完整重建大型商业软件。同时讨论ArtCraft复刻Adobe引发的评级下调，指出数据、云端服务、兼容性和生态锁定仍是护城河。对AI Agent、开源工具和软件商业模式均有参考价值。
-   📰AI 学会拆软件了，闭源软件靠「看不懂」守了二十年的墙，开始漏风了 文章聚焦 GitHub 爆火项目 REA：它把逆向分析工具接入 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 AI 编程智能体，可拆解原生程序、Electron、APK 等，被用于 AI 辅助复刻闭源软件和净室重写。案例包括一人用 AI 复刻 Photoshop/Office 开源替代，以及 AnyPS5 等项目。Quarkslab 实验则显示强混淆仍能拖慢 Agent，法律和云端服务端壁垒也未被突破。核心议题是 AI Agent 正抬高逆向工程效率，可能削弱闭源软件靠“看不懂”建立的护城河。

title: A physics-guided hybrid model for core body temperature estimation: Thermoregulation model with residual learning
summary: Accurate, non invasive estimation of core body temperature (Tc) is vital for real time physiological monitoring and heat illness prevention, yet gold standard measurements are invasive and impractical for wearables. We propose a physics guided hybrid framework that embeds a two node thermoregulation model within a neural residual learning pipeline. The physical layer uses heart rate (HR) to estimate metabolic heat production and directly incorporates wearable head skin temperature, while the residual learner (1D-CNN/LSTM/GRU) corrects systematic model discrepancies. Evaluated on a controlled dataset with strict participant-level splits, the Hybrid-CNN (full input) achieved the best overall accuracy (RMSE (Formula presented) ∘C, MAE (Formula presented) ∘C, (Formula presented) ), outperforming CNN/LSTM/GRU-only networks, an Extended Kalman Filter (RMSE (Formula presented) ∘C), and a physics-only baseline (RMSE (Formula presented) ∘C, negative R2). A simplified Hybrid-CNN that omits ambient sensors performed similarly (RMSE (Formula presented) ∘C, (Formula presented) ), indicating deployability with just HR and skin temperature.
